title: Chapter 559
paragraphs: Chapter 559
Episode 147. The Black Sea King, Gliek (3)
Ron's back was heaving with heavy breaths. His trembling legs, his body thinner than ever, and the ash-colored pattern of his defeated king's sword showed how severe his physical condition was.
"Sir Ron!"
Ron didn't look back but swung Rashid again, spreading sword winds. The grey sword wind slowed down Gliek's falling swords and spears.
It wasn't just Ron who blocked Gliek's path to protect Jin.
Lu Yan, Aquita Hairan, Erol Raimon, Bel Altemiro, Franz.
The five Sword Saints of Hairan were also standing by Ron's side, aiming their swords at Gliek.
They too had exhausted their remaining energy in the face of the onslaught of chaos, enabling Ron to reach Jin.
The Sword Saints standing beside Ron were motionless. After paving the way for Ron, they met death in their tracks.
That was the real end of the Sword Saints.
'The Sword Saints...!'
Hss, whoosh...
Broken and shattered, it was impossible to know how they could fight until this point.
The bodies of the Sword Saints were turning into ash and scattering.

It felt like his chest was being carved by a blade. They thought the long ongoing battle was saying goodbye, but the Sword Saints devoted everything to Hairan and those who served Hairan until the very end.
When the Sword Saints disappeared with a sweep, Ron was left alone to guard the front line.
Everyone was looking at Ron's back.
That's why no one knew what his face looked like.

Tears, sweat, and blood mixed and flowed between the deep wrinkles around his eyes, and from his mouth wide open in emptiness, the sound of him sobbing as he barely suppressed his sorrow seeped out like the wind.
The Sword Emperor Castle was completely shattered, and his grandson, who was more precious than life itself and who had been the reason for his life, was devoured by that monster.
In the end.
Ron Hairan, nearly everything he had loved and protected all his life had gone to a distant place out of reach of the living. A place he could never see or touch again.
And as always.
Despair does not give humans time to grieve. Gliek was swinging hundreds of arms all around, as if he had no interest in Ron's sorrow. Most of them were aimed at where Jin was.
Kaaa, Ahh...!
Ron's howl, carried by his fury, was similar to Dante's voice, roughened by the innate sorrow and despair.
Revenge was demanding.
He was exhausted, and the newly appeared enemy was too large.
He couldn't even ignore Gliek and fight a final battle against Zipfel and the traitors.
Nevertheless, there was only one reason why he didn't give up and stood here to fight again.
If it ended like this, he wouldn't be able to see his grandson's face even in death. However, there was still something left to protect, and his grandson's favorite friend had fought for him.
As an adult, he had to save him and send him away. He couldn't just leave him to die on this barren land, even if he couldn't repay the favor.
The ash-colored radiance of Rashid intensified.
Alone, Ron was deflecting over 70% of Gliek's falling blades towards Jin. The rest were blocked by Stal, the Black Knights, and Jin himself.
'Does he still have such power left, still...!'
Kelliark Zipfel, he had no choice but to be shocked once again while watching Ron running around like a beast from afar.
It should end, but it doesn't end, it should die, but it doesn't die, it should stop, but it doesn't stop.

Ron's battle against Gliek was now clearly beneficial to Kelliark, but Zipfel's members were constantly being overwhelmed by the knights of Hairan. Kelliark and Octavia had also felt an inexplicable anxiety from Ron and the swordsmen.
Even though he was using the magic stone, he was unable to easily move above ground. Although his pure power was far superior, it was meaningless.
Although Ron was a bit closer to Gliek, Kelliark knew that even if he were in that spot, he wouldn't have reached the ground faster than him.
Moreover, if he were Ron, Kelliark would have continued fighting with Zipfel in some way instead of rushing towards Gliek to save Jin. Even if it's a shortcut to mutual destruction.
Unlike Zipfel, which has the goal of completing the magic stone, what lies between Hairan and Jin is just loyalty and righteousness.
Even if he had made the choice to save Jin, it would not have been for loyalty, but for future negotiations with Zipfel.
'Anyway, thanks to your stubborn character, I can relax for now. Please hold on until we and Runcandel can properly join.'
Kelliark formed the 2nd form of Destruction Flame Jade while targeting the ground. His pure flame, not mixed with the power of the magic stone, was dispelling the chaos.

Rosa and Runcandel, Octavia and even the phantom demon were opening a way from the back to save Jin. Even when Rosa saw the defenseless backs of Octavia and the phantom demon from afar, she did not order an attack.
It was time to join forces.
'Even if Sir Ron is blocking, it's only a matter of time before all the comrades die at this rate.'
Since the attack was focused on him from the start, he had to leave for the safety of his comrades.
But changing positions was a gamble. There was no guarantee that Gliek would completely neglect this side if he left his position.
'It's better than just taking it.'
However, he tried a test before moving. He deliberately amplified the spirit of Bradamante to observe Gliek's reaction.
[Sol... Derret...!]
Gliek showed a more ferocious attack as soon as Jin's spirit was amplified.
"Murakan!"
"Yes!"
"I'll draw his attention, you protect Tess and the other comrades. Until Talaris's recovery is complete!"
"Damn it, understood!"
As Jin began to sprint with all his might, Ron and the black knights followed behind him.
Fortunately, Gliek immediately changed his gaze. The swords and spears of chaos were all moving towards the direction Jin was moving.
"You did well, Jin. I was momentarily absorbed in my admiration and forgot about your comrades."
At Ron's words, Jin felt something hot surging up his throat.
"Sir Ron, don't say such things. Rather, your body."
"I won't die until I save you. Even if that monster gets tired of me, I will stubbornly hold on."
Kuguruk-! Cheong!

The seven swords of the knights clashed non-stop with Gliek's weapons. It was a scenario where Ron's sword wind was supporting everyone, just like in the early part of the second battle, and it seemed that they could hold on safely until reinforcements arrived.
However, this feeling was only momentary.
"Are you... belittling... me, Solderet!"
Because he woke up in an incomplete state, it seemed that Gliek recognized Jin not as a contractor but as Solderet himself.
"Cough!"
At the same time, Ron, who had blocked five swords, bent his waist and spat out a black blood clot.
Jin, Stal, and the black knights quickly filled his gap, but their balance was disrupted.
Gliek's means of attack were not limited to hundreds of swords and spears. As soon as Ron lost his center momentarily, a tremendous force of attraction was being generated from Gliek.
Naturally, the one Gliek was trying to pull in with the power of chaos was Jin.
Stal exploded with energy and caused a counterforce, but he couldn't stop Jin from being drawn into the void.
Following Gliek's gaze, Jin levitated in the air. Tess, who confirmed his figure belatedly, gasped.

If the overwhelming power contained in the blue painting did not suppress Gliek's attraction, Jin would have been dragged right in front of Gliek. Fortunately, he stopped halfway, and Jin made eye contact with Gliek.
His trembling eyes seemed like an endless void. Amidst the feeling of being sucked in just by looking, Jin focused his mind and gripped his sword.
Dante.
The monster that swallowed his friend. Deeper and darker hatred was leading to the fear of power that overwhelmed the greatest warriors of the century alone.
[Now, I see.]
Squeak.
Gliek's mouth tore like a crescent moon.
[Solderet, you, seems, to have lost... your strength.]
"You damned monster, what did you do to Dante?"
[He was a... remarkable... human. Somehow... Solderet, was he your contractor?]
"What...?"
"[If I hadn't imitated your voice, it would have been more troublesome......]"
It felt as if something hit his head, and a sharp tinnitus rang in the back of his skull.
He could intuitively understand without needing a detailed explanation. The fact that Dante, while fighting Gliek in the seal of chaos, was tricked by hearing his own voice in some situation.
"......Then what happened to Dante? Is he still inside that seal?"
He asked with a barely calm voice.
"[You keep asking... pointless... questions... Solderet. It's strange, you should... know best.]"
"I don't know."
[Extinction.]
Jin's eyes widened.
[He has ceased to exist.]
"Nonsense."
[Now... it's, your turn.]
"Tess!"
The moment Gliek was about to move, Jin shouted Tess's name and sent his will to him. It was a command to withdraw the pressure.
'Sir Ron needs to create an opportunity to attack.'
Getting Ron to save him only led to more losses in the battle.
'Even if I go in deeper, Tess can pull me out once. I've only been on defense, I need to make at least one successful attack.'
As if a taut line had been cut, when the pressure was withdrawn, Jin's body flew back to Gliek. Hundreds of giant blades formed a dark forest.
It felt like just grazing one would cut off a limb. Jin twisted and turned his body this way and that, reached Gliek's eye, and plunged his sword straight in.
Thunk...!
However, Gliek seemed to be unaffected by the direct stab to his eye.
"Kak!"
Rather, it was Jin who took the hit. The moment he stabbed the eye, one of Gliek's swords slashed across Jin's chest.
His spiritual armor didn't shatter, but his entire body shook as if every bone was about to break.
Gliek tried to slash at the falling Jin once more, but just as Jin wanted, Ron had already dived into his arms and was swinging his sword.
And the moment he fell to the ground and spat out blood, Jin.
He had no choice but to look back at the moment when Gliek's sword hit him.
'Before the sword touched my body, I felt it. It was definitely a force that would remain even after my spiritual armor shattered.'
Just before slashing Jin.
As if someone had pulled it, Gliek's sword tip stopped for a moment.
'Could it be.'
Thump, thump, thump!
His heart pounded like crazy. It was because he thought that what made Gliek hesitate at that moment might have been Dante.
